question: If interest be compounded half - yearly, then find the compound interest on ₹8,000 at 20% p.a. for 1 year.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly** compounding, the rate becomes **half** (20% ÷ 2 = 10%) and time **doubles** (1 × 2 = 2 periods).

Using the **Successive Percentage** formula for 2 periods of 10%:

Effective Rate = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = **21%**

Compound Interest = 21% of 8,000 = 8,000 × 21/100 = **₹1,680**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹8,000, Annual Rate (R) = 20%, Time (T) = 1 year.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ; CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2034bb2cb1bdf8e20076a9431cc5757c97c00e3cd5c60246ad897093605418a5.png] 

⇒ Half-yearly rate (r) = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% per half-year.

⇒ Number of half-years (n) = 1 × 2 = 2.

⇒ A = 8,000 × (1 + 10/100)²

⇒ A = 8,000 × (11/10) × (11/10)

⇒ A = 8,000 × 1.21 = ₹9,680

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P = 9,680 − 8,000

⇒ CI = ₹1,680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate for Half-Yearly Compounding

If the annual rate is R, the effective annual rate for half-yearly compounding is [ (1 + R/200)² − 1 ] × 100.

CI vs SI for 2 Periods

The difference between CI and SI for 2 periods is P × (r/100)², where r is the rate per period.

Compounding Frequency

For quarterly compounding, divide the annual rate by 4 and multiply the time in years by 4 to get the number of periods.
